title: SDK support: Shadow Experiment management APIs (Python/TS/Go) + examples
creator: Monica Patel
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Background
- Shadow Experiments are the primary Console/Rollouts surface for enabling shadow traffic and viewing quality deltas. The Console backend now exposes CRUD + query endpoints, but beta customers are asking for automation (create/stop experiments from CI, export deltas, correlate to rollout IDs).
- Goal: ship first-class SDK bindings in Python/TypeScript/Go for the Shadow Experiments API, aligned with Redwood’s standard client patterns (auth, retries/backoff, pagination, error mapping), plus minimal end-to-end examples.

Scope (v1)
1) Bindings for Shadow Experiments resources
- Create/Update/Delete Shadow Experiment
- Get Shadow Experiment by id
- List Shadow Experiments (filter by route_id, rollout_id, status, time range)
- Start/Stop (if modeled as state transition endpoints; otherwise PATCH state)

2) Query endpoints
- Get aggregates: metric deltas + confidence intervals + sample sizes
- List runs/intervals (if exposed) with time window + segment filters
- Fetch sampled examples (redacted): request/response pair references + rubric outcomes

3) Consistency requirements
- Naming + shape should match other SDK surfaces (e.g., Experiments/A-B APIs) where possible.
- Pagination must be consistent with existing Redwood SDK conventions:
  - Python: iterator + page params
  - TS: async iterable where supported; otherwise page-based list
  - Go: explicit List(ctx, params) returning items + next_cursor
- Error mapping:
  - 4xx validation -> typed ValidationError where available
  - RBAC -> PermissionDenied
  - Feature flag / not enabled -> NotEnabledError (or generic 403 with message) with docs pointer
- Retries: follow existing SDK defaults (retry idempotent GET/LIST; do not retry POST create unless idempotency key is supported).

Out of scope (v1)
- Customer-managed eval code execution or plugin system
- Auto-generated client from OpenAPI if it requires major SDK refactor (we can revisit after beta)
- Bulk export tooling beyond a minimal example script (CSV export is OK in examples)

API assumptions / open questions
- Endpoints are provided by Console backend (ENG-5407). We’ll align with the latest contract and keep a compatibility shim until the beta contract freezes.
- Confirm whether sampled examples are returned inline (redacted) or as pre-signed artifact links; SDK should support both without breaking changes.
- Confirm whether rubric_version is required on create or inferred; if inferred, SDK should surface it on read.

Deliverables
- Python SDK: new ShadowExperiments client + typed models + docstrings + example script
- TypeScript SDK: types + client methods + example Node script
- Go SDK: structs + methods + example program
- Short docs snippet (in SDK READMEs) referencing the main quickstart and retention/redaction warnings.

Acceptance criteria
- All three SDKs can:
  1) Create an experiment for a given route_id and one shadow target
  2) Poll for aggregates and print a human-readable delta summary (metric_name, control, candidate, delta, CI, n)
  3) List a small set of sampled examples (or artifact refs) and print rubric outcomes
- SDK methods are covered by unit tests (request building, pagination, error mapping) and at least one live-ish integration test in nightly (can be mocked server + contract fixtures if needed for private tenants).
- Examples run against internal dogfood tenant behind feature flag and are gated to avoid leaking data.

Implementation notes
- Feature gating: examples must include a preflight check that the tenant has shadow experiments enabled; fail with actionable message.
- Redaction: examples should not print full prompt/response by default; print ids + short excerpts only.
- Stability: mark the SDK surface as “beta” (annotation/tag in docs) until GA contract freeze; avoid breaking names between languages.

References
- Console API implementation: sources/github/redwood/pr-24933-console-api-shadow-experiments-crud.json
- Python SDK PR: sources/github/redwood-sdk-python/pr-1289-add-shadow-experiments-client.json
- TypeScript SDK PR: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-904-add-shadow-experiments-types-and-methods.json
- Go SDK PR: sources/github/redwood-sdk-go/pr-622-shadow-experiments-api-bindings.json
- Draft contract: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/shadow-experiments-api-contract-draft.json
- Docs quickstart: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-511-shadow-traffic-quality-metrics-quickstart.json

Risks / mitigations
- Contract churn during beta: keep a small adapter layer in each SDK that maps renamed fields (e.g., shadow_target_id vs candidate_variant_id) and add deprecation notes.
- Pagination/cardinality: SDK examples should filter narrowly (route_id + short time windows) to avoid encouraging high-cardinality queries.
- Security/PII: examples and docs must emphasize retention defaults and that sampled examples are redacted; point to retention/redaction policy doc.

Rollout plan
- Ship SDK support behind the existing shadow traffic feature flag.
- Enable for internal dogfood tenant first; validate end-to-end against real aggregates.
- Expand to beta Dedicated customers after Console team confirms contract freeze for beta cohort.
